articles.description: Preston revival continues in 4-0 thrashing of Cardiff Scott Parker still waiting for first win at Hammers Will Lankshear was back among the goals as Middlesbrough cemented their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 win over Swansea . Having been restored to the starting lineup at the Riverside, the Championship’s leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to re-establish his side’s lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku’s driven finish had cancelled out Myles Peart-Harris’ opener. articles.title: Manchester City 2-2 Napoli, Real Madrid 5-1 PSV: Champions League clockwatch – as it happened
articles.description: Manchester City were frustrated again while Jude Bellingham inspired Real Madrid to go goal crazy in the second half There’s been a shot on target now, and it’s only gone in! It’s from a corner – one of those where the defender ushers the ball out of play thinking he’s about to get a goal-kick only for the fourth official to point to the corner – from which Yilmaz heads goalwards, the ball loops up off Jackson, and Deniz Gul heads it in! Not only that, just after he does so he gets volleyed in the face by Nicolas Jackson, who was a bit late in trying to clear the ball. The two early kick-offs are now into their 75th minute, and still none of the four teams have had a shot on target. Galatasaray and Aston Villa are currently drawing 2-2 on shots off target and 0-0 on actual goals, while Bodo/Glimt and Lask are drawing 3-3 on shots off target and 0-0 on actual goals. articles.author: Nick Ames at the Etihad Stadium
articles.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
articles.description: For reasons best known to those eyeing the pound signs, Manchester City gave a debut to a special rust-coloured kit in front of a nonplussed crowd. It was of a piece with their performance for most of a familiarly frustrating night that at least concluded with a shot of energy, the home side belatedly shaking off their torpor and ending the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne. Despite the relief sparked by a fine equaliser by Rayan Cherki, who was rewarded for an insistent but hitherto fruitless evening’s endeavours when his angled shot flashed past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, it was hard to see this as anything but a perfect snapshot of their autumn difficulties. Nobody could pretend City were up against crack opposition in a one-paced Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and lack the brio of old, but they simply cannot keep the door shut and could not have quibbled about departing with a defeat. Continue reading...

articles.author: Ed Aarons at Emirates Stadium
articles.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
articles.description: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday , this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, racking up 30 shots by the final whistle. The German side had to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember, although Arteta admitted his players must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight. Continue reading...

articles.author: Bryan Armen Graham
articles.title: Gukesh escapes time crisis to draw world chess championship opener with Sindarov
articles.description: Opening game ends in draw by repetition Defending champion plays white in Game 2 Read our move-by-move report of Game 1 Sindarov: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’ Indian chess star Gukesh Dommaraju held off Javokhir Sindarov amid a mounting time crisis on Tuesday, drawing the opening game of their eagerly awaited $2.5m world title match in 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the picturesque Geneva suburb of Cologny. After spending more than 36 minutes on a single move and much of the afternoon racing against the clock, the defending champion said the time he invested early helped him play faster as a drawish position sharpened and his minutes dwindled opposite the in-form Uzbek challenger . “When I got into the time trouble, I’d already thought about the next few moves,” Gukesh said. “And then the moves after that were pretty easy.” Continue reading...

articles.author: Ben Fisher at Rams Park
articles.title: Gul takes pain for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
articles.description: This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with different emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, the scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph , or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s match-winner, Deniz Gul, finished with similar, the substitute requiring a bandage after bravely taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as the hosts rippled the net on 77 minutes. It was the game’s first effort on target, Galatasaray maintaining their commanding form on home soil to extend Villa’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. On the outside, this is a gladiatorial arena, a giant spaceship parked on Ali Sami Yen complex. But inside there is a poor pitch that began cutting up during the warm-up. John McGinn, one of four changes from Villa’s stalemate with Sunderland on Saturday, gestured towards the turf in frustration after a through ball went awry, but nobody of a Villa persuasion could blame defeat on the surface. As Unai Emery had stated, it was the same for both teams. Continue reading...

articles.description: Playmaker in best form since moving to Anfield ‘I am really enjoying playing under Iraola’ Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025. The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult debut season under Arne Slot and also struggled in the early weeks of Iraola’s reign. Wirtz scored an exquisite improvised goal in the 4-0 defeat of Manchester United on Sunday when he also created 10 chances from open play. Continue reading...

articles.author: Press Association
articles.title: Jannik Sinner’s Australian Open appearance in doubt after knee surgery
articles.description: Wimbledon champion sidelined since winning title ‘We’ve tried everything to treat injury without surgery’ Jannik Sinner faces further time off the court after undergoing knee surgery. The former world No 1 has been sidelined with pain in his right knee since winning his second consecutive Wimbledon title in July. Details on Sinner’s condition have been scarce but on Tuesday he announced he has had a minor operation on his iliotibial band in an attempt to solve the problem. While no timeline for recovery has yet been set out, it seems almost certain to rule out a comeback for the Australian Open in January, as had been the intention. Continue reading...

articles.author: Gerard Meagher
articles.title: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks
articles.description: Hooker was involved in 2019 win against New Zealand ‘The way we trained today, I don’t see any complacency’ Luke Cowan-Dickie is adamant England will not let complacency creep in after their record win over the All Blacks , insisting they will not repeat the mistakes of the 2019 World Cup. Cowan-Dickie is one of three players, with Jamie George and Maro Itoje, who would claim a fourth career win for England against New Zealand on Saturday if Steve Borthwick’s side back up last weekend’s 37-12 victory at Twickenham. The Sale hooker was part of the squad who defeated the All Blacks in the 2019 World Cup semi-final in emphatic fashion and went into the final against South Africa as favourites. Eddie Jones’s side were comfortably outplayed by the Springboks , however, with Cowan-Dickie acknowledging that England failed to hit their emotional peak that day. Continue reading...

articles.title: Senegal restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions after court ruling
articles.description: Senegal won January’s final 1-0 after walking off Result was overturned in March as 3-0 win for Morocco Senegal have been reinstated as the champions of Africa, and their controversial 1-0 victory against Morocco confirmed in the record books, after the scandal over January’s Africa Cup of Nations final was resolved in a Swiss courtroom. The court of arbitration for sport (Cas) ruled that a decision to award the 2025 Afcon title to Morocco on appeal should be set aside. Senegal celebrated with a social media post proclaiming the team to have won the title twice: first on the field and then at Cas. Morocco, who are due to co-host the World Cup in 2030, declared their intention to “pursue all legal avenues” to challenge the ruling. Continue reading...

articles.title: 'Something switched inside me': Nick Foles on his Super Bowl flow state and move behind the mic
articles.description: As he continues a foray into broadcasting with Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game, the Philadelphia folk hero reflects on fatherhood, flow states and outdueling Tom Brady Ask Nick Foles what he remembers most vividly about winning Super Bowl LII and he doesn’t mention the Philly Special , the brazen gadget play that passed straight into football folklore. Not the record 1,151 yards of combined offense or the nerve-shredding go-ahead touchdown drive or the surreal theater of a second-string quarterback outdueling Tom Brady on the biggest stage in American sports. Not even the moment Brady’s last-gasp Hail Mary pass fell harmlessly to the turf and the Philadelphia Eagles became champions of the National Football League for the first time since the Eisenhower administration. Instead, he remembers holding his daughter. Continue reading...

articles.author: Aaron Timms
articles.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
articles.description: For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Continue reading...

articles.author: Luke Entwistle
articles.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
articles.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says. Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 . “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.” Continue reading...

articles.title: Lights go out on Commanders before they beat Bengals in final seconds
articles.description: Cincinnati Bengals 20-22 Washington Commanders Drew Stevens kicks game-winning field goal Game delayed after lights go out in third quarter Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired, and the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night. After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight-yard line. Daniels spiked the ball again with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest. Continue reading...
